Messages.Author: Dervish
Messages.Body:
Hello All,

I've always liked this card, I played in in the release but since then, it never makes the cut. Anyone have anything good to say about it?

Kingston Penitentiary, Ontario
Type: Master
Cost: 4 pool
Master: unique location. Hunting ground.
During your untap phase, you may move 1 blood from the blood bank to a ready vampire you control. Any other Methuselah may give you a pool during his or her untap phase to tap this card to move 1 blood from the blood bank to a ready vampire he or she controls. A vampire can gain blood from only one hunting ground card each turn.

best,
D

Messages.Author: extrala
Messages.Body:
The card is just too expensive imho.  If you leave the card untapped in order to get a pool, and nobody is willing to utilize it, you have just lost a turn. It may be a good way to keep you in the game, if one of your crosstable buddies is giving you pool each turn, but for the cost of 4 pool it's going to pay off only after 5 turns. So why spend the 4 pool upfront at all?  I think a good alternative text would be that the controller of the card can the tap card to gain blood on one of his vampires in any untap or discard phase, so that you wouldn't loose a turn if nobody is willing to give you the pool.

I have never seen the card being played iirc.

Messages.Author: elotar
Messages.Body:
Math is smth like this:

2 pool for hunting ground (generic, which is good, but HG, which is not so good)

2 pool for "gain 1 pool sometimes" effect.

You need at least 3 such "sometimes" to get profit.
"Sometimes" may, imo, happen only if said metusela got vamp with no blood and does't want to hunt. In half cases it will be your prey or predator, so you will suffer more, than you gain, so for real profit you need 7-8 such "sometimes".

So it's very unlikely.

NC Russia

Messages.Author: TorranceCircle
Messages.Body:
I've only seen this card played a few times, sometimes by me, but the real problem with this card, as I see it, is that you have no control over who usess it. For example, the few times I've seen it played it was left unused by other methuselahs until that one turn when they needed a blood so they would not have to hunt. Then, they proceed to bleed you for three for the oust. Or something else that sets them up for the GW. I seem to remember this happening 50% of the time. 4 pool is too much to pay when that lack of control comes with it. Owain gives you control and this creates bargaining options for you. I could see it having some value for a parity shift deck but other than that it is a real gamble to put on the table, IMHO.

edit: I wonder if it appears in the TWD? If so how many times?

Messages.Author: Haze
Messages.Body:
I got to use it once, with a tremere combat deck. unfortunately I got out-combatted and couldn't drain my prey's vampires. I think it only got me 1 pool from my grand-predator, as a "don't get ousted" pity gift.

Unless you're losing 4 pool to play Parity Shift, you probably need to engineer a situation where vampires are low on blood. Young Bloods, Hunger Moon, combat, stuff like that. preferably forcing your prey to tap it to oust them faster. You may not be able to control who uses it, but sometimes it's okay to let your prey get a blood so they can keep their forward pressure. just don't let them oust.

it's 2 pool for the HG effect, so if other players use it twice you've at least broken even. if it's your prey, only once is still not bad (you paid 1 extra and your prey lost 1)

also consider that it's one of the three generic hunting grounds any clan (e.g. bloodlines) can use, next to Club Zombie (4 pool) and Threestar Cab Company (3 pool). if you feel like you need a HG in the first place, it's got to compete with those two.

alternate "protection racket" strategy: slap it on the table. find a suitable player to threaten every turn. if they don't give you a pool, you're gonna rush their best vampire to torpor.

Messages.Author: bakija
Messages.Body:
> Dervish wrote:
> I've always liked this card, I played in in the release but since then, it never makes the cut. Anyone have anything good to say about it?
>
Yeah, I can't imagine that it sees much actual play. I mean, granted, there is one actually in play in one of the JOL tournament games I'm in currently, played by some sort of pot/ani/Anarch weenie deck, but the deck doesn't seem to be doing so hot, so I can't imagine that the Funky Kingston is going to help much.

At 4 pool for a non clan hunting ground that might gain you a pool once and a while, it is just not a good card. In theory, as it could gain you all sorts of pool (due to people paying you a pool every turn around the table to give their guy a blood), but I can't imagine that someone will pay you that pool particularly often. I'd imagine that gaining 1 pool from Funky Kingston a game would be on the top end of the "does that ever actually happen?" curve. And I suspect that most games, it won't gain you any pool at all, at which point it is just a 4 pool hunting ground.

Having it in Parity Shift decks (as noted) might be worth doing, but Club Zombie is probably a generally better bad master card that costs 4 pool. And a Secret Horde (assuming you can count) is generally better than either for this particular purpose.

Maybe in some sort of hilarious Santaleous (the guy who gets +1 bleed for each HG in play) deck?

Yeah, Funky Kingston is just a mostly bad card.
